uncited: Voxel-to-Image Slicing is a technique for rendering 3D voxel data in raster-based renderers (specifically Cycles) by converting raw volumetric data into a 2D tiled EXR image.
Each tile in the image represents a 2D slice of the volume along the Z-axis, allowing the renderer to access 3D data via 2D texture sampling.
It differs from standard 3D texture sampling by flattening the volume into a 2D grid of slices, which requires specific coordinate mapping logic to resolve 3D coordinates to 2D image pixels.
- **Input:** Raw byte buffer of size $N = \text{res}_x \times \text{res}_y \times \text{res}_z$, containing density values (typically 8-bit unsigned integers).
- **Pixel Array:** A 1D array of size $\text{width} \times \text{height}$, where each element is a 4-component float vector $[R, G, B, A]$.
- $\text{numColumns} = \lceil \sqrt{\text{res}_z} \rceil$ if `multiRow` is true; otherwise $\text{numColumns} = \text{res}_z$.
- $\text{numRows} = \lceil \text{res}_z / \text{numColumns} \rceil$ if `multiRow` is true; otherwise $\text{numRows} = 1$.
- $\text{width} = (\text{res}_x + 1) \times \text{numColumns}$.
- $\text{height} = (\text{res}_y + 1) \times \text{numRows}$ if $\text{numRows} > 1$; otherwise $\text{height} = \text{res}_y$.
Read the raw byte buffer of size $\text{res}_x \times \text{res}_y \times \text{res}_z$.
Calculate tile grid dimensions ($\text{numColumns}, \text{numRows}$) based on `multiRow`.
Create the image with calculated width and height, setting `is_data=True`.
Read the value $v$ from the buffer at index $p$.
If the buffer is 8-bit unsigned int, convert to float: $v_{float} = v / 255.0$.
*(Note: The source code assigns the same value to R, G, and B channels.
If true, splits slices into a 2D grid of tiles to reduce coordinate inaccuracies for large slice counts.
- **Memory Usage:** Large voxel datasets cause high memory usage.
- **Coordinate Inaccuracy:** Single-row tile layouts cause inaccuracies as the number of slices grows large.
If the input format differs, the conversion $v/255.0$ must be adjusted.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(\text{res}_x \times \text{res}_y \times \text{res}_z)$ for the conversion process.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(\text{width} \times \text{height})$ for the pixel array.
- **Limitations:** High memory consumption for large volumes; single-row layout suffers from precision issues; not suitable for real-time rendering due to conversion overhead.
This method was developed for use in Blender's Cycles renderer to allow raw volumetric data (such as from MRI scans or smoke simulations) to be visualized.
It was adapted from a Smoke2EXR add-on to handle general voxel data.
The technique addresses the limitation that images are inherently 2-dimensional, requiring a mapping strategy to represent 3D volumes.
